verdict.rationale: Codex Plugins ships a built-in `@plugin-creator` skill that the assistant runs to scaffold plugins. Installed plugins and skills let users hand tasks to the Codex/ChatGPT assistant, such as summarizing Slack channels, drafting replies, sending messages on their behalf, or opening PRs via an explicitly invoked skill. The assistant itself is the host Codex/ChatGPT agent rather than something the plugin layer provides, so credit rests mainly on the documented built-in skills and plugin workflows. Missing for 10: evidence of an assistant that belongs to the plugin product itself rather than the host, hands-on corroboration of end-to-end delegation, and documentation of how delegated tasks are tracked or completed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: For the fastest setup, use the built-in `@plugin-creator` skill. It scaffolds the required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest and can also generate a local marketplace entry for testing.
The plugin-creator skill will create the plugin folder, create the required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, and add MCP server wiring for the plugin.
Install the Slack plugin to summarize channels or draft replies.
it can read and search iMessage, SMS, and RCS chats on your Mac and send messages on your behalf through the Messages app
You can also invoke them explicitly, e.g. "use the PR skill to open a PR."
